author: Declaration Desk
title: India bowled out for 89 as Henry's six wickets give New Zealand a 244-run win
dek: Will Young's 125 led New Zealand to 333 at Bay Oval before Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and Shreyas Iyer all fell for ducks. India lead the series 2-1 with one match left.
body:
New Zealand beat India by 244 runs in the fourth one-day international at Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui, on Friday, bowling the visitors out for 89 after making 333. Fast bowler Matt Henry took six wickets for 27 runs, and India's top order collapsed in the opening overs.

The result cuts India's lead in the five-match series to 2-1, with the final game at the same ground on Sunday. India cannot lose the series, but New Zealand can level it.

## How the match went

India's captain, Shreyas Iyer, standing in for Shubman Gill, who has joined India's Test squad, won the toss and chose to bowl. It was the eighth time in nine matches on the tour that India had won the toss, according to reports.

Opener Will Young was dropped twice in successive balls on 5, once at slip and once by the wicketkeeper, according to reports, and went on to make 125 from 108 balls with 14 fours and four sixes, his fifth ODI century and his first against India. He put on 85 for the first wicket with Tim Seifert, who made 58 from 48 balls, and Finn Allen added 41 from 30. Captain Mitchell Santner made 24 from 29 balls late on, and New Zealand were bowled out for 333 in the final over, their fourth-highest first-innings total against India, according to one report. Henry and Fisher were both run out.

Axar Patel was India's most economical bowler, taking 2 for 39 in his ten overs. Auqib Nabi took 2 for 59 and Gurnoor Brar 2 for 69.

The chase fell apart at once. Henry took three wickets in the first over, according to reports: Rohit Sharma edged his first ball to slip, Virat Kohli was bowled and Iyer was out leg before wicket after a review. All three were out without scoring. Ruturaj Gaikwad made 5, and India were 22 for 4 after nine overs. Ishan Kishan top-scored with 27, and no partnership of note followed. Matthew Fisher took 3 for 31 to support Henry.

## The series so far

India won the first match in Auckland by five wickets and the second, in Wellington, by four runs on the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method. The third, also in Wellington, was washed out without a ball bowled. India had already won the five-match T20 series 3-2 earlier in the tour.

## Why it matters

The defeat is a jolt for an Indian side, without Gill, that had looked in control of the tour. Sunday's match is now a decider for the series result rather than a dead rubber. For New Zealand, it is a first ODI win of the series after two defeats and a washout.

## What happens next

The fifth and final ODI is on Sunday, 15 November, at Bay Oval. A New Zealand win would square the series at 2-2; India need a win or a no-result to take it.
